speaker: Unknown
en: Fighting slop with slop.
zh: 用劣质代码对抗劣质代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: My name is Vaibhav, and I'm going to talk about something that is a little, I would say, maybe a little silly at first.
zh: 我叫 Vaibhav，我要讲的东西，我想说，一开始可能有点傻。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to show you our team's engineering practices really quickly.
zh: 我要非常快地向你们展示我们团队的工程实践。

speaker: Unknown
en: We do no-code reviews, we require every engineer to work on things in parallel, and we have no standardization in how people do AI.
zh: 我们不做代码审查，我们要求每个工程师并行工作，而且我们在人们如何做 AI 方面没有任何标准化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I know immediately what almost all of you are thinking.
zh: 我立刻就知道你们几乎所有人都在想什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're probably a Zoom or YC startup.
zh: 我们可能是一家 Zoom 或 YC 创业公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I can guarantee you I'm clearly a millennial.
zh: 我可以向你保证，我显然是一个千禧一代。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what do we actually do at our company without code reviews?
zh: 那么在没有代码审查的情况下，我们在公司实际上做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, about three years ago, we decided to build a programming language.
zh: 嗯，大约三年前，我们决定构建一种编程语言。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's something that has absolutely no room for slop.
zh: 这是一个绝对没有劣质代码余地的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's something that has to work every single time exactly the same way.
zh: 这是一个每次都必须以完全相同方式工作的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's something that you can't just change a year later or a month later because you made a bad design decision.
zh: 这是一个你不能因为做了一个糟糕的设计决定就在一年后或一个月后更改的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to be correct.
zh: 你必须正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for the last three years, we've been in an onslaught of war against slot.
zh: 在过去三年里，我们一直处于一场对抗劣质代码的战争攻势中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when I first met this enemy, I went to my great mentor, Slop Sue, and he taught me something.
zh: 当我第一次遇到这个敌人时，我去找我伟大的导师 Slop Sue，他教了我一些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: To defeat the slop, we must become the slop.
zh: 为了击败劣质代码，我们必须成为劣质代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we began, and we prepared, and then we started winning.
zh: 于是我们开始，我们准备，然后我们开始获胜。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when we think about it, what is slop?
zh: 所以当我们思考这个问题时，什么是劣质代码？

speaker: Unknown
en: Slop is just any code you don't read.
zh: 劣质代码就是任何你不阅读的代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: And whether any of you admit it or not, this is the least amount of slop that your code base will ever have.
zh: 无论你们承不承认，这都是你们的代码库曾经拥有的最少量的劣质代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: Cherish it.
zh: 珍惜它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we started fighting back against the slop, and we started fighting back with slop.
zh: 所以我们开始反击劣质代码，我们开始用劣质代码反击。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how do we go ship a stable programming language with these engineering practices?
zh: 那么我们如何通过这些工程实践发布一个稳定的编程语言呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, the first skirmish we ever had was the skirmish of standards.
zh: 嗯，我们遇到的第一次小冲突是标准之战。

speaker: Unknown
en: The hard part about hiring great engineers is you sadly can't tell them what to do.
zh: 雇佣优秀工程师的困难部分在于，遗憾的是你不能告诉他们该做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Some of them want to use Claude, some of them want to use Codex, some of them want to use the latest thing that they just found on Hacker News.
zh: 他们中的一些人想使用 Claude，一些人想使用 Codex，一些人想使用他们刚刚在 Hacker News 上发现的最新东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So instead of trying to hold standards in our code base, we did something that is an invariant.
zh: 因此，我们没有尝试在代码库中保持标准，而是做了一件不变的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: We built an architecture.md file.
zh: 我们构建了一个 architecture.md 文件。

speaker: Unknown
en: Instead of using ClaudeMD, just pick something that every model can just understand.
zh: 不要使用 ClaudeMD，只需选择每个模型都能理解的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: This file has to be incredibly small, and it can only have things that will not change for months or for years.
zh: 这个文件必须非常小，并且只能包含几个月或几年内不会改变的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: In our case, it's the layers of the compiler.
zh: 在我们的例子中，它是编译器的层。

speaker: Unknown
en: You go deeper into the compiler, tell the agent to just talk to at least one other person.
zh: 深入编译器，告诉智能体至少与另一个人交谈。

speaker: Unknown
en: That slows it down a little bit.
zh: 这让它慢了一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now we have standards so anyone can use whatever they want.
zh: 所以现在我们有了标准，任何人都可以使用他们想要的任何东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the real foe we faced was actually the battle of design.
zh: 但我们面临的真正敌人实际上是设计之战。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone here knows that you have to write perfect design docs.
zh: 这里的每个人都知道你必须编写完美的设计文档。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we have a very simple rule in our team.
zh: 我们团队有一个非常简单的规则。

speaker: Unknown
en: Code can be slopped, writing cannot.
zh: 代码可以是劣质的，写作不能。

speaker: Unknown
en: And of course, if I tell every engineer this, they write beautiful writing, and they handwrite everything, they don't use AI.
zh: 当然，如果我告诉每个工程师这个，他们会写出漂亮的文字，并且他们手写所有东西，他们不使用 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, sadly not.
zh: 嗯，遗憾地并非如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we built a design doc tool.
zh: 所以我们构建了一个设计文档工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: What this design doc tool does, it's a replacement for both Notion and GitHub effectively for design docs.
zh: 这个设计文档工具的作用，实际上是 Notion 和 GitHub 在设计文档方面的替代品。

speaker: Unknown
en: It allows versioning, commenting, all the stuff you want.
zh: 它允许版本控制、评论，以及你想要的所有东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And obviously we do this, people use this.
zh: 显然我们要这样做，人们使用这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, sadly not.
zh: 嗯，遗憾地并非如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: We built another tool on top of that.
zh: 我们在那个基础上又构建了一个工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this tool was a Slack integration for that tool.
zh: 这个工具是那个工具的 Slack 集成。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every time a design doc got updated, this channel got notifications.
zh: 每次设计文档更新时，这个频道都会收到通知。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what ended up happening is this channel became the most popular channel in our company really fast.
zh: 最终发生的是，这个频道很快成为我们公司最受欢迎的频道。

speaker: Unknown
en: At 2 a.m., someone shipped a new design doc, three people started reading it right away because it's just interesting.
zh: 凌晨 2 点，有人发布了一个新的设计文档，三个人立刻开始阅读它，因为它很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: The most interesting stuff is design docs that are not going to change.
zh: 最有趣的东西是不会改变的设计文档。

speaker: Unknown
en: But this wasn't enough.
zh: 但这还不够。

speaker: Unknown
en: All of this is actually backed by markdown files and simple CLI scripts that make it treat like GitHub without being GitHub itself.
zh: 所有这些都实际上由 markdown 文件和简单的 CLI 脚本支持，这些脚本使它表现得像 GitHub 而本身不是 GitHub。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now agents can go do this.
zh: 所以现在智能体可以去做这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the real problem with all this is I built this and I hit a little bit of AI psychosis.
zh: 但所有这一切的真正问题是我构建了这个，并且我遇到了一点 AI 精神错乱。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I started shipping 10 design docs a day.
zh: 我开始每天发布 10 个设计文档。

speaker: Unknown
en: And soon, the team was fighting my slop.
zh: 很快，团队就在对抗我的垃圾内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have to go back at the last rule.
zh: 所以我们必须回到最后一条规则。

speaker: Unknown
en: This last rule was if you're going to ship a design doc, you require people to actually go read it.
zh: 这最后一条规则是，如果你要发布一个设计文档，你需要人们真正去阅读它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with this last standard, we suddenly had design docs that are incredibly high quality.
zh: 有了这最后一条标准，我们突然有了质量极高的设计文档。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what about the battle of architecture?
zh: 但是架构之战呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you have your code base converge?
zh: 你如何让你的代码库收敛？

speaker: Unknown
en: We built another tool.
zh: 我们构建了另一个工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: This tool basically visualizes our dependency graph internally with some external dependencies as well and allows us to watch the code base change.
zh: 这个工具基本上可视化了我们内部的依赖关系图，还有一些外部依赖，并允许我们观察代码库的变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: It has semantic boundaries, individual packages, but what's more interesting is we can go build CLI tools that guarantee that certain invariants can't be broken.
zh: 它有语义边界、独立的包，但更有趣的是我们可以构建 CLI 工具来保证某些不变量不会被破坏。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what this does is when Claude builds a new package or adds a dependency that's leaky, we now have CI CD changing or a simple git commit history that tells us exactly where things break.
zh: 它的作用是，当 Claude 构建一个新包或添加一个有泄漏的依赖时，我们现在有 CI CD 变更或简单的 git 提交历史告诉我们确切哪里出问题了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by this, we're actually able to make our architecture change.
zh: 通过这个，我们实际上能够使我们的架构发生变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: We haven't changed our architecture in the last three or four months.
zh: 在过去三四个月里我们没有改变我们的架构。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as much as we might do design docs, and as much as we might have stable code, would you genuinely ship code without reading it?
zh: 但是尽管我们可能会做设计文档，尽管我们可能有稳定的代码，你会真正地在没有阅读代码的情况下发布代码吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Would you trust your team to go do that?
zh: 你会信任你的团队去那样做吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And think about a programming language.
zh: 想想一种编程语言。

speaker: Unknown
en: A programming language has so many invariants.
zh: 编程语言有那么多不变量。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have generics, you have closures, you have memory allocation, you have FFI boundaries.
zh: 你有泛型，你有闭包，你有内存分配，你有 FFI 边界。

speaker: Unknown
en: Could you trust that system?
zh: 你能信任那个系统吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Python has bugs 25 years later.
zh: Python 在 25 年后仍有 bug。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, here's where we did something slightly different.
zh: 好吧，这就是我们做了一些略有不同的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: What we did was we built a system that actually has agents constantly running and creating BAML programs.
zh: 我们做的是构建了一个实际上有智能体不断运行并创建 BAML 程序的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: We take these BAML programs.
zh: 我们获取这些 BAML 程序。

speaker: Unknown
en: One second.
zh: 等一下。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we have agents try and spin something up from scratch.
zh: 我们有智能体尝试从头开始启动一些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: We then look at the entire Claude transcript, see what tools it used, see what happened, and obviously we as humans can inspect them, but more importantly, we can have agents go inspect them.
zh: 然后我们查看整个 Claude 对话记录，看看它使用了什么工具，看看发生了什么，显然我们人类可以检查它们，但更重要的是，我们可以让智能体去检查它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And agents find what was good, what was bad.
zh: 智能体发现什么是好的，什么是坏的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And not just what was bad in terms of what was incorrect in the language, but what took three tool calls when it should have only taken one.
zh: 不仅仅是语言中什么是错误的方面，还有什么是本应只需一次工具调用却用了三次的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we can go ahead and find issues, and we can have humans collaborate with these issues to figure out which ones are real, which ones are hallucinations, which ones don't have taste, as much as I hate to use that word.
zh: 然后我们可以继续发现问题，我们可以让人类与这些问题协作，以弄清楚哪些是真实的，哪些是幻觉，哪些没有品味，尽管我很讨厌使用那个词。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we can have agents go ahead and create fixes to these problems and go to address them.
zh: 然后我们可以让智能体继续创建针对这些问题的修复并去解决它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And most importantly, instead of trying to just detect these issues, we can go one step further.
zh: 最重要的是，除了试图仅仅检测这些问题，我们可以更进一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: What if you could find language features, and instead of guessing what was good, guessing what skill was good, you could go and A-B test it.
zh: 如果你能找到语言特性，并且不用猜测什么是好的，不用猜测什么技能是好的，而是去 A-B 测试它，会怎么样？

speaker: Unknown
en: You could figure out which ones took less tool calls, which one made less errors, which one produced the correct outcome, and deterministically know what's going on.
zh: 你可以弄清楚哪些使用了更少的工具调用，哪个犯了更少的错误，哪个产生了正确的结果，并确定性地知道发生了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: The point is, you can start building data-driven systems without ever writing a single line of code.
zh: 关键是，你可以开始构建数据驱动的系统，而无需编写一行代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the thing that really I care about the most over here
zh: 我在这里真正最关心的东西

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not that any one of these tools is specifically what you should go build.
zh: 并不是说这些工具中的任何一个具体是你应该去构建的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the fact of the matter is, in order to build a programming language, it wouldn't have taken eight people.
zh: 但事实是，为了构建一种编程语言，它不会需要八个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It wouldn't have taken less than two years.
zh: 它不会需要不到两年的时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: It would have taken hundreds and thousands and tens of thousands of man hours, and then you would still have a broken system.
zh: 它会花费成千上万个工时，然后你仍然会有一个破损的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And today, we can just spend billions of tokens and make it work, and we can make it stable.
zh: 而今天，我们可以只花费数十亿的 token 并让它工作，我们可以让它稳定。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you too can go home and build these internal tools and these sloppy tools to make sure that your code bases can ship without really having to read necessarily every single line of code, because your engineers aren't going to.
zh: 你也可以回家构建这些内部工具和这些粗糙的工具，以确保你的代码库可以在不需要真正阅读每一行代码的情况下发布，因为你的工程师不会去读。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we can start winning this battle against slop.
zh: 我认为我们可以开始赢得这场对抗垃圾内容的战斗。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as we win this battle, slop can be defeated.
zh: 当我们赢得这场战斗时，垃圾内容可以被击败。

speaker: Unknown
en: But sadly, I have a sad thing to say.
zh: 但遗憾的是，我有一件悲伤的事情要说。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we're still going to lose the war.
zh: 我认为我们仍然会输掉这场战争。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the reason that we're gonna lose this war is because some of the foundational stuff that we try and go use itself is broken.
zh: 我认为我们将要输掉这场战争的原因是，我们要尝试去使用的一些基础性东西本身就已经坏了。

speaker: Unknown
en: How many of you have used TypeScript?
zh: 你们有多少人用过 TypeScript？

speaker: Unknown
en: Probably most of you hopefully at this point, or at least your agents have, so something around there.
zh: 希望你们大部分人现在都用过，或者至少你们的智能体用过，差不多是这样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Did you know that TypeScript's main design goal is to strike a balance between correctness and productivity?
zh: 你们知道 TypeScript 的主要设计目标是在正确性和生产力之间取得平衡吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's an asterisk here, because what they really mean is human productivity.
zh: 这里有一个星号，因为他们真正的意思其实是人类的生产力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if you think about it, there are things you would never do in a programming language at the very core layer if you were designing in a world where humans never wrote a single line of code.
zh: 如果你仔细想想，有些事情你在编程语言的最核心层是永远不会去做的，如果你是在一个人类从未写过一行代码的世界里进行设计的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me show you what that really means.
zh: 让我展示一下那到底是什么意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm gonna write something and try and guess what this code does.
zh: 我要写点东西并试着猜猜这段代码是做什么的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pretty safe.
zh: 很安全。

speaker: Unknown
en: What about this one?
zh: 这个呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or even more so, this one.
zh: 或者更有甚者，这个呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why do we turn things to strings when we sort them?
zh: 为什么我们在排序时要把东西转成字符串？

speaker: Unknown
en: This is just slop baked into the language, whether you like it or not.
zh: 这就是烘烤进语言里的垃圾，不管你喜欢不喜欢。

speaker: Unknown
en: What about this?
zh: 那这个呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: I love this part of TypeScript.
zh: 我喜欢 TypeScript 的这一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you know what my agent loves?
zh: 你们知道我的智能体喜欢什么吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: This part of TypeScript.
zh: TypeScript 的这一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is slop baked into the language.
zh: 这就是烘烤进语言里的垃圾。

speaker: Unknown
en: And whether you like it or not, the systems will have slop.
zh: 不管你喜欢不喜欢，系统里都会有垃圾。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you build using these tools.
zh: 如果你使用这些工具进行构建的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, I'm sorry, wrong talk.
zh: 哦，抱歉，搞错演讲了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you think about what JavaScript does, JavaScript exists, and then after JavaScript existed, we started building systems to layer it on.
zh: 但如果你想想 JavaScript 做了什么，JavaScript 存在着，然后在 JavaScript 存在之后，我们开始构建系统将其分层叠加。

speaker: Unknown
en: We built CoffeeScript, then TypeScript, and now we're trying to build Effect.
zh: 我们构建了 CoffeeScript，然后是 TypeScript，现在我们正试图构建 Effect。

speaker: Unknown
en: But thing is, the thing underneath is already broken.
zh: 但问题是，底层的东西已经是坏的了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And more so, the way we write code is also different now.
zh: 而且，我们现在写代码的方式也不同了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So why are we trying to patch something like this?
zh: 那为什么我们还要试图修补像这样的东西呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Why don't we just try and do something a little different?
zh: 为什么我们不试着做点稍微不同的事情呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think what we might need if we try and go do that is basically going to be a made-up language.
zh: 我认为如果我们尝试那样做，可能需要的基本上是一种编造出来的语言。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let me show you what BAML really can do.
zh: 所以让我展示一下 BAML 真正能做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you start thinking from first principles, how you can try and combat slop from a very foundational layer itself.
zh: 以及当你开始从第一性原理思考时，你如何尝试从最基础的层面本身去对抗垃圾。

speaker: Unknown
en: I keep talking about not reading code.
zh: 我一直在谈论不阅读代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does it even matter?
zh: 这真的重要吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, let me show you a new way to think about code.
zh: 好吧，让我给你展示一种思考代码的新方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this isn't to say we all have to go do this right away.
zh: 这并不是说我们都得立刻这样去做。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what if every single time I looked at code, what if every single time I looked at code, what I really saw was not the code itself, but a quick little thing that could actually visualize all the code for me?
zh: 但是如果每一次我查看代码时，如果每一次我查看代码时，我真正看到的不是代码本身，而是一个快速的小东西，它能为我可视化所有的代码，会怎样？

speaker: Unknown
en: As I clicked around, it took me to exact lines of code that I was linked to.
zh: 当我四处点击时，它会带我来到我链接到的确切代码行。

en: And remember, this is the least amount of slop your code base will ever have to this day.
zh: 请记住，这是你的代码库直到今天所必须拥有的最少量的混乱。

zh: 我认为我们都可以构建一个拥有美丽软件的世界。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think what it takes is I want each of you to go home today and build these sloppy tools, make your systems more robust, make your processes more robust.
zh: 我认为这需要你们每个人今天回家后去构建这些混乱的工具，让你们的系统更健壮，让你们的流程更健壮。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then for the bravest of you, I want you to go back and think about these core foundation layer systems.

en: Think about how they're broken and see if you can imagine a way to fix them.
